svg.title: Weight-only and weight-activation quantization target different GPU bottlenecks
svg.desc: W4A16 stores weights in 4-bit and keeps activations in 16-bit, dequantizing inside the kernel before a 16-bit matrix multiply — this cuts memory traffic for memory-bound decode but leaves compute-bound prefill unchanged. W8A8 or FP8 stores both weights and activations in low precision and multiplies them directly on tensor cores with no dequantize step, which speeds compute-bound prefill only on hardware and kernels that support native low-precision math.

text.font-family: Space Grotesk, IBM Plex Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: How weight and activation quantization differ

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: W4A16 shrinks the bytes the GPU must move for decode.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: W8A8/FP8 lets supported tensor cores compute in low precision directly.

svg.text: Compute-bound prefill wants W8A8/FP8 with matching hardware

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: Weight-only cuts the bytes moved from VRAM; the matmul itself still runs at the old precision.

svg.text: Weight-activation removes the dequantize step, but only pays off with native low-precision tensor cores.
